concepts.def: Combining elements from different musical traditions, as in Paul Simon's 'Graceland' (1986) with South African mbaqanga.
Texture where multiple performers play simultaneous variations of the same melody, common in Middle Eastern traditions.
Use of intervals smaller than a semitone, characteristic of Arabic maqam and Indian raga systems.
Antiphonal exchange between leader and group, fundamental to West African musical traditions and gospel.
Simultaneous combination of contrasting rhythms, particularly developed in sub-Saharan African drumming.
Music passed down by listening and imitation rather than notation, the primary transmission mode for most world musics.
